instructions: Bihar STET Paper 2 Computer Science practice mock test.

questions.question: What is 3/4 of 20?
Which action most directly reduces single-use plastic waste?

options.text: Using durable reusable containers where practical

questions.explanation: Reuse reduces demand for disposable items; safe local recycling can also help.

questions.question: A process in the ready state is:

options.text: Waiting for an I/O event only

questions.explanation: Ready processes can run when scheduled but are not currently executing.

questions.question: Which property is associated with TCP but not guaranteed by UDP?
questions.explanation: TCP provides reliable, ordered byte-stream delivery; UDP does not guarantee it.

questions.question: For a sparse graph, which representation often uses less space?

options.text: A full n×n table in all cases

questions.explanation: Adjacency lists use O(V+E) space, advantageous when E is much smaller than V².

questions.question: A person walks 4 km north, then 3 km east. The straight-line distance from the start is:
questions.explanation: The path forms a right triangle: √(4²+3²)=5 km.

questions.question: Which Python object is immutable?
questions.explanation: A tuple's item bindings cannot be reassigned, though it may contain mutable objects.

questions.question: What is the value of 7 / 2 when both operands are int in C?
questions.explanation: Integer division discards the fractional part for positive operands.

questions.question: A candidate key is:

options.text: Any attribute used in a query

questions.explanation: It uniquely identifies tuples and is minimal with respect to that property.

questions.question: An analytic rubric differs from a holistic rubric because it:

options.text: Is used only for multiple-choice tests

questions.explanation: Analytic rubrics report performance across distinct criteria.

questions.question: A well-written instructional objective should primarily describe:
questions.explanation: Objectives should state what learners will be able to demonstrate.

questions.question: A student should protect an account by:

options.text: Using a unique strong password and multi-factor authentication where available
Using the same simple password everywhere

questions.explanation: Unique passwords and MFA reduce account-compromise risk.

questions.question: Which cloud service model gives the customer the most control over the guest operating system?
questions.explanation: IaaS provides virtualized infrastructure while customers manage guest OS and applications.

questions.question: Which relational algebra operation combines tuples from two relations based on a condition?
questions.explanation: A join combines related tuples from relations.

questions.question: In C, modifying the same scalar object multiple times without sequencing in one expression can cause:

options.text: A compile-time syntax error in every case

questions.explanation: Unsequenced conflicting side effects can make behavior undefined.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the four Coffman conditions?
questions.explanation: The four are mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and circular wait.

questions.question: In operant conditioning, reinforcement is a consequence that:

options.text: Increases the future likelihood of a behavior
Has no relation to behavior frequency

questions.explanation: Reinforcement is defined by its effect on behavior probability.

questions.question: Which protocol resolves an IPv4 address to a link-layer MAC address on a local network?
questions.explanation: ARP discovers the MAC address associated with a local IPv4 address.

questions.question: A requirement describing response time is usually classified as:
questions.explanation: Performance constraints are non-functional requirements.

questions.question: Which clause filters groups after aggregation?
questions.explanation: HAVING applies conditions to grouped/aggregated results.

questions.question: A firewall is primarily used to:

options.text: Filter network traffic according to rules
Guarantee that no malware can run
Encrypt every file on a disk automatically

questions.explanation: Firewalls enforce traffic policies; they are not a complete security solution.

questions.question: Find the next term: 3, 7, 15, 31, __.
questions.explanation: Each term is previous × 2 + 1, so 31 × 2 + 1 = 63.

questions.question: Method overloading is typically resolved using:

options.text: Runtime object type only in all languages
Method name and parameter signature at compile time

questions.explanation: Overload resolution commonly uses parameter lists at compile time.

questions.question: In A* search, the evaluation function is commonly:
questions.explanation: A* combines path cost so far g(n) with heuristic estimate h(n).

questions.question: Differentiated instruction means:

options.text: Giving every learner exactly the same support regardless of need
Adjusting support or task pathways while maintaining learning goals

questions.explanation: Differentiation responds to readiness, interest or learning needs.

questions.question: Lossless compression guarantees that:

options.text: The reconstructed data is identical to the original
The file is always smaller than with lossy compression
Only audio files can be encoded

questions.explanation: Lossless methods preserve all original information after decompression.

questions.question: A 4-to-1 multiplexer requires how many select lines?
questions.explanation: Two select bits choose one of four inputs.

questions.question: Which statement about a structure variable is correct?

options.text: All members share one storage location
Members have separate storage within the structure, subject to padding
Every structure must be dynamically allocated

questions.explanation: Each member has its own storage; padding may be inserted for alignment.

questions.question: Binary search requires which key condition on a typical array implementation?

options.text: Array length is a power of two

questions.explanation: Binary search discards half the search interval based on sorted order.

questions.question: A teacher notices that one group is rarely heard during discussion. The best first response is to:

options.text: Use structured turn-taking and varied participation formats
Assume the group has nothing to contribute
Stop asking the group questions permanently
Grade participation only by speaking volume

questions.explanation: Structures can widen participation and reduce dominance by a few voices.

questions.question: Which scheduling algorithm can cause starvation of low-priority processes?

options.text: Round robin with equal time slices

questions.explanation: A continuously arriving stream of higher-priority work can starve low-priority jobs.

questions.question: What is the value of i after `int i=0; while(i<3) i++;`?
questions.explanation: The loop increments i until it reaches 3, then stops.

questions.question: A relation is in 2NF when it is in 1NF and has no:

options.text: Transitive dependency of non-key attributes on a key
Partial dependency of a non-prime attribute on a candidate key

questions.explanation: 2NF removes partial dependencies of non-prime attributes on candidate keys.

questions.question: A B+ tree is widely used for database indexes because it:

options.text: Stores all records only in internal nodes
Supports balanced search and efficient range access

questions.explanation: Balanced structure and linked leaves support efficient lookups and range scans.

questions.question: A pipeline hazard caused by an instruction needing a result not yet produced is:
questions.explanation: A dependency on an unavailable result creates a data hazard.

questions.question: A router primarily forwards packets using:
questions.explanation: Routers use network-layer destination information and routing tables.

questions.question: A digital signature primarily provides:

options.text: Integrity, origin authentication and non-repudiation support

questions.explanation: Signatures verify a message against a signing key and help establish integrity and origin.

questions.question: A hypothesis is best described as:

options.text: A conclusion that can never be revised
A list of observations without a claim

questions.explanation: A hypothesis can be tested against evidence.

questions.question: Which OSI layer is responsible for end-to-end transport services?
questions.explanation: The transport layer provides process-to-process delivery services.

questions.question: The ratio 12:18 in simplest form is:
questions.explanation: Divide both terms by their greatest common divisor, 6.

questions.question: A 4-bit binary counter can represent how many distinct states?
questions.explanation: Four bits represent 2^4 = 16 states.

questions.question: A cold boot usually means:

options.text: Starting the computer from a powered-off state

questions.explanation: Cold boot begins from a powered-off condition.

questions.question: A NAND gate produces 0 only when:
questions.explanation: NAND is the complement of AND, so only input 11 gives output 0.

questions.question: For teaching a procedure that requires repeated practice and feedback, the most suitable approach is often:
questions.explanation: Demonstration plus guided practice makes the steps visible and allows feedback.

questions.question: In most expressions, an array name is converted to:

options.text: A pointer to its first element
A pointer to its last element

questions.explanation: Array-to-pointer conversion commonly yields a pointer to element zero, with exceptions such as sizeof.

questions.question: Which operation removes the top element from a stack?
questions.explanation: Pop removes the current top element.

questions.question: Which statement about Unicode and ASCII is correct?

options.text: ASCII defines more characters than Unicode
Unicode assigns code points to characters across many scripts
Unicode uses exactly 7 bits for every character
ASCII and Unicode are identical standards

questions.explanation: Unicode provides a much broader character repertoire; encodings such as UTF-8 represent its code points.

questions.question: What does a function prototype primarily provide?

options.text: Declaration of function name, return type and parameter types

questions.explanation: A prototype enables type checking at calls before the definition is encountered.

questions.question: A recursive function must have a base case primarily to:
questions.explanation: A reachable base case prevents unbounded recursive calls for valid inputs.

questions.question: A collision in a hash table occurs when:

options.text: Two keys map to the same table index
The table contains only one key
The hash function returns a negative number only

questions.explanation: Different keys may hash to the same index.

questions.question: Which HTML element represents a self-contained composition that could be independently reusable?
questions.explanation: The article element represents a self-contained composition.

questions.question: A lesson plan is most useful when it aligns objectives, learning activities and:
questions.explanation: Alignment makes assessment evidence relevant to intended learning outcomes.

questions.question: If int x=10; int *p=&x; then *p refers to:
questions.explanation: Dereferencing p accesses the object it points to, namely x.

questions.question: Which practice is most likely to support intrinsic motivation?

options.text: Using meaningful choice and explaining task relevance

questions.explanation: Autonomy and relevance can strengthen internal engagement.

questions.question: The zone of proximal development concerns tasks a learner can do:

options.text: With guidance but not yet independently
Without prior knowledge in every case

questions.explanation: ZPD is the gap between independent performance and performance with support.

questions.question: In a simple electric circuit, current is measured in:
questions.explanation: The ampere is the SI unit of electric current.

questions.question: A preventive classroom-management strategy is to:

options.text: Wait until disruption occurs before setting any rule

questions.explanation: Clear routines prevent confusion and reduce avoidable disruptions.

questions.question: Which relationship is most directly modeled by inheritance?
questions.explanation: Inheritance commonly models an is-a specialization relationship.

questions.question: For F(A,B)=Σm(1,3), the simplified expression is:
questions.explanation: Minterms 01 and 11 share B=1, so F=B.

questions.question: Positive transfer occurs when prior learning:

options.text: Facilitates learning or performance on a new task
Has no relationship to any new task

questions.explanation: Positive transfer means previous learning helps with a new situation.

questions.question: For int a[5], the last valid index is:
questions.explanation: C arrays use zero-based indexing, so indices are 0 through 4.

questions.question: The Constitution of India came into effect on:
questions.explanation: It came into effect on 26 January 1950; adoption occurred on 26 November 1949.

questions.question: A learning management system is primarily used to:

options.text: Organize course materials, activities, submissions and feedback
Encrypt every network packet by itself

questions.explanation: An LMS supports the administration and delivery of learning activities.

questions.question: Which printer type forms characters by striking an inked ribbon?
questions.explanation: Dot-matrix printers are impact printers that strike a ribbon.

questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to A + AB?
questions.explanation: By the absorption law, A + AB = A.

questions.question: Which language class is recognized by finite automata?
questions.explanation: Finite automata recognize exactly the regular languages.

questions.question: For a learner with low vision, which adjustment is most directly helpful?

options.text: Providing readable enlarged text and appropriate contrast

questions.explanation: Accessible print and contrast improve access while preserving learning goals.

questions.question: Which function moves the file-position indicator to a specified location?
questions.explanation: fseek changes the file-position indicator.

questions.question: Wait time after asking a question can help because it:

options.text: Gives learners time to process and formulate answers
Guarantees every answer will be correct
Only benefits learners who already know the answer

questions.explanation: Adequate thinking time can improve response quality and participation.

questions.question: Text-to-speech software most directly supports learners who benefit from:

options.text: Replacing all written assessment for everyone

questions.explanation: Text-to-speech converts digital text into spoken output.

questions.question: In a singly linked list, deleting a known non-head node generally requires:

options.text: Updating the previous node's next pointer

questions.explanation: The predecessor must bypass the deleted node.

questions.question: A greedy algorithm makes a choice that is:

options.text: Locally attractive at each step under its strategy
Deferred until all solutions are enumerated

questions.explanation: Greedy methods choose locally best options; correctness requires a suitable problem property.

questions.question: Which body conducts elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies in India?
questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India administers these elections.

questions.question: An interrupt allows the processor to:

options.text: Respond to an event by suspending current flow and invoking a handler

questions.explanation: The CPU saves suitable state and transfers control to an interrupt handler.

questions.question: The 'D' in ACID stands for:
questions.explanation: Durability means committed changes persist despite failures.

questions.question: An exit ticket used to adapt tomorrow's lesson is an example of:
questions.explanation: It provides evidence during learning to guide next instructional steps.

questions.question: A value rises from 80 to 100. The percentage increase is:
In a neural network, weights primarily determine:

options.text: The file format of training data

questions.explanation: Weights are parameters adjusted during training.

questions.question: A teacher who discovers a grading error should:

options.text: Correct it transparently using the same fair criteria
Hide it to avoid extra work
Discuss the student's private information publicly

questions.explanation: Transparent correction protects fairness and trust.

questions.question: The worst-case time complexity of insertion sort is:
questions.explanation: Reverse-sorted input causes a quadratic number of shifts/comparisons.

questions.question: Testing a module in isolation is called:
questions.explanation: Unit testing checks a small component independently.

questions.question: Effective feedback is most useful when it is:

options.text: Specific, timely and linked to an actionable next step

questions.explanation: Specific actionable feedback helps learners improve their work.

questions.question: Which storage class gives a local variable static storage duration?
questions.explanation: A local static variable retains its value between function calls.

questions.question: A test consistently measures the wrong construct. It may be:
questions.explanation: Consistency is reliability; measuring the intended construct is validity.

questions.question: Which organ primarily filters blood to form urine?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter blood and regulate water and electrolyte balance.

questions.question: A DFA has, for each state and input symbol:

options.text: An arbitrary set of next states

questions.explanation: A deterministic transition function maps each state-symbol pair to one state.

questions.question: Which algorithm finds shortest paths from one source when all edge weights are non-negative?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm assumes non-negative edge weights.

questions.question: Which component translates a virtual address to a physical address during execution?
questions.explanation: The Memory Management Unit performs address translation.

questions.question: A cache hit ratio is 0.9. If hit time is 2 ns and miss penalty adds 20 ns, approximate AMAT is:
questions.explanation: AMAT ≈ hit time + miss rate × miss penalty = 2 + 0.1×20 = 4 ns.

questions.question: A Java class can directly implement:

options.text: No interfaces if it extends a class

questions.explanation: Java permits a class to implement multiple interfaces.

questions.question: Encapsulation is best described as:

options.text: Deriving a class from another class
Bundling state and behavior while controlling access
Calling multiple methods with one name only
Converting source code to machine code

questions.explanation: Encapsulation combines data and operations and supports access control.

questions.question: Which compiler phase commonly detects whether identifiers are declared and used consistently?
questions.explanation: Semantic analysis checks scope, types and declaration-related constraints.

questions.question: A context-free grammar has productions whose left-hand side is:

options.text: Any string of terminals and nonterminals

questions.explanation: A CFG production has a single nonterminal on its left-hand side.

questions.question: The Quit India Movement was launched in:
questions.explanation: The movement began in August 1942.

questions.question: Thrashing is most closely associated with:
questions.explanation: Thrashing spends substantial time swapping pages rather than executing useful work.

questions.question: The hexadecimal digit A represents which decimal value?
questions.explanation: Hexadecimal digits A through F represent decimal 10 through 15.

questions.question: Which CSS property controls the space inside an element's border?
questions.explanation: Padding is the space between content and border.

questions.question: A typical RISC design emphasizes:

options.text: A relatively small set of simple instructions
Executing all instructions in microcode only

questions.explanation: RISC designs typically favor simpler instructions and efficient pipelining.

questions.question: A file descriptor is typically:

options.text: A small integer handle used by a process to access an open file

questions.explanation: Unix-like systems use file descriptors as per-process handles for open files and I/O objects.

questions.question: Book is to reading as fork is to:
questions.explanation: A fork is commonly used for eating, as a book is used for reading.

questions.question: A full adder has how many input bits, including carry-in?
questions.explanation: It adds A, B and carry-in, producing sum and carry-out.

questions.question: Assimilation occurs when a learner:

options.text: Interprets new experience using an existing schema
Changes a schema to accommodate conflicting information
Copies a behavior after punishment only

questions.explanation: Assimilation fits new information into existing cognitive structures.

questions.question: In Scrum, a sprint is:

options.text: A fixed-length iteration producing a usable increment

questions.explanation: A sprint is a time-boxed development iteration.

questions.question: What is the 8-bit two's-complement representation of -5?
A memory contains 4096 addressable locations, each 16 bits wide. Its capacity is:
questions.explanation: 4096 × 16 bits = 65536 bits = 8192 bytes = 8 KiB.

questions.question: A question asking students to compare two solutions and justify a choice primarily assesses:
questions.explanation: Comparison and justification require reasoning beyond recall.

questions.question: DNS primarily translates:

options.text: Domain names to resource records such as IP addresses

questions.explanation: DNS resolves names to records, commonly including IP addresses.

questions.question: Which function releases memory obtained through malloc?
questions.explanation: free returns dynamically allocated storage to the allocator.

questions.question: A parser primarily consumes:

options.text: Machine code and emits source code

questions.explanation: Parsing determines whether the token stream conforms to grammar rules.

questions.question: How many usable host addresses are available in a conventional IPv4 /27 subnet?
questions.explanation: A /27 leaves 5 host bits: 2^5 − 2 = 30 usable addresses.

questions.question: In-order traversal of a binary search tree visits keys in:

options.text: Ascending order for the usual BST ordering

questions.explanation: Left-root-right traversal yields sorted order in a BST.

questions.question: If a lesson is running behind, the teacher should first:

options.text: Prioritize the essential objective and adapt lower-priority activities
Rush through every task without explanation
Ignore learner questions in every case

questions.explanation: Protecting the core objective is better than mechanically completing every activity.

questions.question: Which Java construct is intended to run whether or not an exception is thrown, in ordinary try-finally flow?
questions.explanation: finally is used for cleanup and normally runs as control leaves the try statement.

questions.question: Statements: All coders are learners. Some learners are artists. Which conclusion definitely follows?
questions.explanation: The first statement directly guarantees that all coders are learners; the overlap with artists is not guaranteed.

questions.question: Two students disagree during group work. A constructive teacher response is to:

options.text: Guide them to describe the issue and agree on fair next steps
Immediately decide one student is always at fault
Remove all group work for the whole term

questions.explanation: Structured dialogue helps students resolve conflict and practice social skills.

questions.question: Which circuit stores one bit of state?
questions.explanation: A flip-flop is a bistable storage element.

questions.question: Which gas is a major anthropogenic greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide from fossil fuel use and land-use change contributes to warming.

questions.question: Photosynthesis uses light energy to help plants produce:

options.text: Glucose from carbon dioxide and water

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water to form sugars, releasing oxygen.

questions.question: The principle of least privilege means users should receive:

options.text: Only permissions necessary for assigned tasks

questions.explanation: Least privilege limits access to what is needed for the role.

questions.question: Which directive is used for conditional compilation?
questions.explanation: The #if family controls conditional inclusion during preprocessing.

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm is stable in its standard merge-sort implementation?
questions.explanation: Merge sort can preserve the relative order of equal keys.

questions.question: A compiler symbol table commonly stores:

options.text: Identifier attributes such as type and scope

questions.explanation: Symbol tables support identifier lookup and semantic checks.

questions.question: If an algorithm performs 3n²+5n+2 basic operations, its asymptotic time complexity is:
questions.explanation: The highest-order term dominates asymptotically.

questions.question: A constructivist teacher is most likely to:

options.text: Help learners build understanding through prior knowledge and active inquiry
Treat learners as passive recipients only

questions.explanation: Constructivism emphasizes active meaning-making and prior knowledge.

questions.question: DMA is primarily used to:

options.text: Transfer blocks between I/O and memory with limited CPU involvement

questions.explanation: Direct Memory Access transfers data without the CPU handling every word.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer passes through which country?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer crosses several Indian states.

questions.question: Before sharing a claim found on social media, a learner should first:

options.text: Check the source and corroborate it with reliable evidence
Forward it because it is popular
Trust it if it has an image
Ignore the publication date and author

questions.explanation: Verification and corroboration reduce misinformation sharing.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is generally intended to retrieve a representation without changing server state?
questions.explanation: GET is defined as a safe retrieval method in normal use.

questions.question: The TCP three-way handshake is:
questions.explanation: The three messages establish synchronized connection state.

questions.question: A hypervisor is software that:

options.text: Manages virtual machines on host hardware

questions.explanation: Hypervisors create and manage virtual machine execution environments.

questions.question: Universal Design for Learning encourages teachers to provide multiple means of:
questions.explanation: UDL uses flexible pathways for engagement, information access and demonstrating learning.

questions.question: A semaphore is commonly used to:
questions.explanation: Semaphores coordinate concurrent execution and resource access.

questions.question: In immediate addressing, the operand is:

options.text: Stored only in a stack frame

questions.explanation: The instruction contains the literal operand value.

questions.question: C passes ordinary function arguments by:
questions.explanation: The parameter receives a value; pointers can be passed to allow indirect modification.

questions.question: A page fault occurs when:

options.text: A requested page is not currently mapped as present in main memory
A process enters the ready queue

questions.explanation: The OS must resolve a reference to a page that is not resident.

questions.question: In a max-heap, the key at each parent is:

options.text: At least as large as its children

questions.explanation: The max-heap property places a maximum among the root's key and descendants at the root.

questions.question: A schedule is conflict-serializable if its precedence graph is:

options.text: A tree with exactly one root

questions.explanation: Acyclic precedence graphs imply conflict serializability.

questions.question: In an IoT system, a sensor primarily:

options.text: Changes digital data into a physical action
Measures a physical condition and produces a signal

questions.explanation: Sensors observe physical phenomena such as temperature or motion.

questions.question: Which sequence best describes a basic instruction cycle?
questions.explanation: The processor fetches the instruction, decodes it, then executes it.

questions.question: When most learners answer the same concept question incorrectly, the teacher should:

options.text: Revisit the concept using a different explanation and check understanding again
Assume the class did not study and move on
Lower the passing mark without teaching
Repeat the exact same explanation louder

questions.explanation: A common error is evidence to adjust instruction and reassess.

questions.question: Active listening is best demonstrated by:

options.text: Paraphrasing the speaker's point and asking a relevant clarifying question
Preparing a reply while ignoring the speaker

questions.explanation: Paraphrasing and clarification show attention and check understanding.

questions.question: Biodiversity refers to variation among:

options.text: Living organisms, including within species and ecosystems

questions.explanation: Biodiversity includes genetic, species and ecosystem diversity.

questions.question: What does len({'a':1, 'b':2}) return in Python?
questions.explanation: len on a dictionary returns the number of keys.

questions.question: Inflation generally refers to:

options.text: A sustained rise in the general price level
A fall in all prices every day
An increase in one person's salary only
A decrease in money supply by definition

questions.explanation: Inflation is a sustained increase in the overall price level.

questions.question: Corrective maintenance is performed to:

options.text: Adapt software to a new operating system only

questions.explanation: Corrective maintenance addresses defects or failures.

questions.question: Student records should generally be shared:

options.text: Only with authorized people for legitimate educational purposes

questions.explanation: Confidentiality requires appropriate access and purpose limitation.

questions.question: A binary tree with n nodes has how many edges, if n > 0?
questions.explanation: Every non-root node has exactly one parent edge, giving n−1 edges.

questions.question: A circular queue is useful mainly because it:

options.text: Reuses slots freed at the front
Eliminates the need for front and rear indices

questions.explanation: Circular indexing reuses array positions instead of wasting freed slots.

questions.question: The average of 6, 8, 10 and 12 is:
questions.explanation: Their sum is 36; 36 divided by 4 is 9.

questions.question: Overfitting occurs when a model:

options.text: Performs poorly on training and test data equally by necessity
Fits training data well but generalizes poorly to unseen data
Always has high bias and low variance

questions.explanation: Overfitting captures noise or idiosyncrasies that do not generalize.
